front: When does the `else` block of a `for` loop run?
back: When the loop finishes all its iterations without hitting `break`. If `break` ends the loop, the `else` block is skipped.
The `break` fires at `8`, so the `else` block does not run. With only odd numbers it would print `all odd`.
The condition becomes false without a `break`, so the `else` block runs once after the loop. A `while` loop that never runs its body also runs `else`.
`break` leaves the loop at `tries == 2`, so `else` is skipped and only the final print runs.
